newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZCC clears Mercury, Utilicorp NZ buy of Power NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZCC clears Mercury, Utilicorp NZ buy of Power NZ.

text.p: The anti-monopolies New Zealand Commerce Commission said on Friday it had cleared a joint venture between Auckland-based Mercury Energy and Utilicorp New Zealand to acquire up to 100 percent of the shares in Power New Zealand.
Utilicorp NZ is 80 percent owned by Utilicorp United Inc.
Mercury and Utilicorp would each own 50 percent of the joint venture. There are also associated cross shareholdings in Waikato regional power distributor WEL Energy and Bay of Plenty Electricity.

Commerce Commission chairman Alan Bollard said the commission was satisfied the acquisition would not result in any party acquiring or strengthening a dominant position in the relevant electricity markets.
The commission analysed the matter as though Mercury, Power NZ, WEL Energy and Bay of Plenty Electricity were all one entity.
The NZCC had previously cleared Mercury to buy up to 100 percent of the shares in Mercury. That clearance, in 1994, did not involve a joint venture with any other companies.
Power NZ appealed that clearance but the High Court rejected the appeal. Power NZ then appealed to the Court of Appeal, which also rejected it.
The NZCC said the courts' judgments were significant for the whole electicity industry and gave strong support to the way in which the commission viewed business acquisitions in the industry.

Bollard said that although the acquisition would result in aggregation in the national retail market of almost 40 percent, there would still be other powerful players, as well as minor players, in the market.
Both Mercury and Power NZ are electricity distributors in the Auckland market.
